def match(pattern: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """
    Implements a basic regex matching algorithm using recursion and dynamic programming
    to support literal characters, '.', '*' (zero or more of the preceding element), 
    and '+' (one or more of the preceding).
    """
    
    def dp(p_index: int, t_index: int, memo: dict) -> bool:
        if (p_index, t_index) in memo:
            return memo[(p_index, t_index)]
        
        if p_index == len(pattern):
            result = t_index == len(text)
            memo[(p_index, t_index)] = result
            return result
            
        first_match = (t_index < len(text) and
                       (pattern[p_index] == text[t_index] or pattern[p_index] == '.'))
        
        if p_index + 1 < len(pattern):
            if pattern[p_index + 1] == '*':
                result = (dp(p_index + 2, t_index, memo) or
                          (first_match and dp(p_index, t_index + 1, memo)))
                memo[(p_index, t_index)] = result
                return result
            elif pattern[p_index + 1] == '+':
                result = first_match and dp(p_index, t_index + 1, memo) or (first_match and dp(p_index + 2, t_index, memo))
                memo[(p_index, t_index)] = result
                return result
        
        if first_match:
            result = dp(p_index + 1, t_index + 1, memo)
            memo[(p_index, t_index)] = result
            return result
        
        memo[(p_index, t_index)] = False
        return False

    return dp(0, 0, {})
